from_quote: The United States guarantee to every ſtate in the union a ſeparate republican form of government
rationale: The paragraph restates the guarantee clause of Article IV, Section 4 in nearly its words ("guarantee to every state in the union").
to_quote: guarantee to every State in this Union a Republican Form of Government

from_quote: teſt is ever to be required of any officer or ſervant of the United States
rationale: The paragraph says no religious test is ever to be required of any officer of the United States, restating Article VI, Clause 3. The scan prints "religions" before "test"; the quoted words begin after it.
to_quote: no religious Test shall ever be required as a Qualification to any Office or public Trust under the United States

from_quote: The temporary reſervation of any particular matter muſt ever be deemed an admiſſion that it ſhould be done away
rationale: The paragraph discusses the importation of slaves and a "temporary reservation" on the subject, which refers to the clause of Article I, Section 9, Clause 1 that bars Congress from prohibiting it before 1808.
to_quote: The Migration or Importation of such Persons as any of the States now existing shall think proper to admit, shall not be prohibited by the Congress prior to the Year one thousand eight hundred and eight

from_quote: Theſe have been called ex poſt facto laws, and are exploded by the new ſyſtem
rationale: The paragraph names "ex post facto laws" as "exploded by the new system," which refers to the prohibition in Article I, Section 9, Clause 3. Article I, Section 10 also names such laws, as a restraint on the states; the paragraph does not say which it means.
to_quote: ex post facto Law shall be passed

from_quote: In all criminal caſes, where the property, liberty or life of the citizen is at ſtake, he has the benefit of a jury
rationale: The paragraph says that in all criminal cases the citizen has the benefit of a jury, which describes the jury-trial clause of Article III, Section 2, Clause 3.
to_quote: The Trial of all Crimes, except in Cases of Impeachment, shall be by Jury

from_quote: If convicted on impeachment, which is never done by a jury in any country, he cannot be fined, impriſoned or puniſhed, but only may be diſqualified from doing public miſchief by loſing his office
rationale: The paragraph describes the judgment on impeachment as limited to losing office and disqualification, with a further trial for any crime, which is the content of Article I, Section 3, Clause 7.
to_quote: Judgment in Cases of Impeachment shall not extend further than to removal from Office, and disqualification to hold and enjoy any Office

from_quote: when a diſpute ariſes between the citizens of any ſtate about lands lying out of the bounds thereof, or when a trial is to be had between the citizens of any ſtate and thoſe of another, or the government of another
rationale: The paragraph lists the disputes that may go to a federal court: lands outside a state's bounds, and trials between citizens of different states or with a foreign government. These are among the controversies listed in Article III, Section 2, Clause 1.

from_quote: no perſon holding an office under the United States is permitted to enjoy any foreign honors, powers or emoluments
rationale: The paragraph says no person holding an office under the United States may enjoy foreign honors, powers or emoluments, which describes the second part of Article I, Section 9, Clause 8.
to_quote: no Person holding any Office of Profit or Trust under them, shall, without the Consent of the Congress, accept of any present, Emolument, Office, or Title, of any kind whatever, from any King, Prince, or foreign State

from_quote: Two years are the utmoſt time for which the money can be given
rationale: In discussing the power to raise an army, the paragraph says that two years are the longest term for which the money can be given, which is the limit in Article I, Section 8, Clause 12.
to_quote: no Appropriation of Money to that Use shall be for a longer Term than two Years

from_quote: The regulations of theſe elections are, by the firſt part of the clauſe, to be preſcribed by the ſtate legiſlatures
rationale: The paragraph discusses the power of the federal government over elections of Representatives and Senators, the state legislatures' part "by the first part of the clause" and the exception for the places of choosing Senators, all in Article I, Section 4, Clause 1.
to_quote: The Times, Places and Manner of holding Elections for Senators and Representatives, shall be prescribed in each State by the Legislature thereof

from_quote: may chooſe the electors of the Preſident and Vice-Preſident of the Union
rationale: The paragraph says that, unless the state legislatures order otherwise, the people may choose the electors of the President and Vice-President, which describes Article II, Section 1, Clause 2.
to_quote: in such Manner as the Legislature thereof may direct, a Number of Electors

from_quote: the legiſlature of the ſtate will have the election of the Senate
rationale: The paragraph says the state legislature will elect the Senate, which restates Article I, Section 3, Clause 1.

from_quote: the new conſtitution expreſsly declares, that the foederal Repreſentatives ſhall be in the proportion of one to every thirty thouſand
rationale: The note says the Constitution "expressly declares" the proportion of Representatives at one to every thirty thousand, the ratio in Article I, Section 2, Clause 3.
